payload.name: I have a cloned OpenSearch repository that contains anomaly
payload.description:
I have a cloned OpenSearch repository that contains anomaly detection functionality implemented in Java. I want to convert this Java code to Python, but instead of using the OpenSearch Python client, I want to use the Elasticsearch Python library (elasticsearch[async]) with async functionality.

Please help me with:

Understanding the structure of the Java anomaly detection module in the OpenSearch repo (key classes, methods, and logic flow).

Mapping Java constructs to equivalent Python constructs (e.g., streams → list comprehensions, Java types → Python types, error handling, concurrency).

Rewriting the core anomaly detection logic in Python using elasticsearch.AsyncElasticsearch (async client) for:

Connecting to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch

Executing queries

Reading/writing indices

Triggering and retrieving anomaly detection results

Ensuring the Python version supports the same configuration options, thresholds, and detection algorithms as the Java version.

Providing a complete, runnable async Python script (or module structure) with example usage, including:

How to create and configure an AsyncElasticsearch client

How to configure the anomaly detection job

How to feed data / trigger detection asynchronously

How to retrieve and interpret results asynchronously

Showing how to properly run async code (e.g., using asyncio.run(...)) and handle connection errors, timeouts, and backoff.

The OpenSearch repo is already cloned on my system. Assume I can navigate to the relevant Java source files (e.g., under src/main/java/org/opensearch/anomalydetecion/...). If you need specific file paths or class names, ask me for them.

Please output:

A high-level explanation of the Java anomaly detection logic

The equivalent async Python implementation using elasticsearch[async]

Any necessary dependencies (requirements.txt including elasticsearch)

Example async usage code with AsyncElasticsearch

goal.answer: Reimplement the core OpenSearch Anomaly Detection plugin logic in async Python using elasticsearch[async], supporting single-entity and multi-entity streaming anomaly detection against an Elasticsearch cluster. The Python module must replicate the Java behavior: feature aggregation queries, shingling, Random Cut Forest scoring, hybrid thresholding (log-normal + KLL quantiles), anomaly grade assignment, result serialization, and model checkpoint persistence.

criteria.answer:
A runnable async Python module exists that replicates the core anomaly detection flow using elasticsearch[async] to read feature data from ES and write results back.
Python Pydantic data models exist for AnomalyDetector, Feature, AnomalyResult, Entity, IntervalTimeConfiguration, and DetectorInternalState with JSON serialization matching the OpenSearch AD index schemas.
The detection engine supports both single-entity and multi-entity detectors using krcf (Python AWS RCF bindings) for scoring, with custom Python implementations for shingling, imputation, and the HybridThresholdingModel.
HybridThresholdingModel equivalent implemented in Python: log-normal CDF initialization, rank-based grade computation with MIN_SCORE=0.4 threshold, and confidence reporting.
requirements.txt pins elasticsearch[async], krcf, pydantic, numpy, and supporting libraries.
An example asyncio entrypoint script demonstrates: creating the AsyncElasticsearch client, configuring a detector, running detection, and retrieving results with proper timeout/backoff/connection-error handling.
Model checkpoint persistence supported via read/write to an Elasticsearch index (.opendistro-anomaly-checkpoints equivalent) so detection can resume across runs.

phases.answer: Models & Async Client, Core ML Engine, Runner, Multi-Entity & Example

phaseSnapshots.name: Models & Async Client
phaseSnapshots.goal: Establish the Python project foundation with Pydantic models and an async Elasticsearch client wrapper.
phaseSnapshots.description: Create requirements.txt, directory structure, and Pydantic v2 models for AnomalyDetector, Feature, AnomalyResult, Entity, IntervalTimeConfiguration, and DetectorInternalState. Implement an AsyncElasticsearch client factory with configurable hosts, authentication, connection pooling, timeout, and exponential backoff/retry. Also define the index name constants and a utility to ensure index templates/mappings exist.

steps.description: Create directory structure and requirements.txt with elasticsearch[async], krcf, pydantic, numpy.
Implement Pydantic models mirroring the Java classes with correct JSON field aliases.

verification.command: python -c "from src.models import AnomalyDetector, AnomalyResult; print('ok')" exits 0

steps.description: Implement async ES client factory with retry/backoff and index management helpers.

verification.command: python -c "from src.client import create_es_client; print('ok')" exits 0

phaseSnapshots.name: Core ML Engine
phaseSnapshots.goal: Implement feature aggregation, shingling, imputation, RCF scoring, and hybrid thresholding.
phaseSnapshots.description: Build the FeatureManager that constructs and executes async ES aggregation queries to fetch feature data per detection interval. Implement shingle construction (default size 8, max missing proportion 0.25), LinearUniformImputer, and missing-data handling. Integrate krcf RandomCutForest for scoring. Reimplement HybridThresholdingModel in Python with log-normal CDF initialization, KLL-sketch-like quantile tracking (using numpy/scipy approximations or a lightweight quantile estimator), and anomaly grade computation.

steps.description: Implement FeatureManager with async ES feature query and shingle construction.
Implement HybridThresholdingModel with log-normal CDF, quantile sketch, and grade computation.
Integrate krcf RandomCutForest and create a ThresholdedRandomCutForest wrapper that combines RCF scoring with thresholding.

phaseSnapshots.name: Runner, Multi-Entity & Example
phaseSnapshots.goal: Orchestrate end-to-end detection for single and multi-entity detectors with checkpoint persistence and provide a runnable example.
phaseSnapshots.description: Implement AnomalyDetectorRunner that orchestrates: querying features, building shingles, scoring with RCF, thresholding, constructing AnomalyResult objects, and writing results to ES. Add multi-entity support via composite aggregation queries and per-entity model state management. Implement checkpoint DAO for persisting/restoring RCF model state and thresholding model state to ES. Write example script with asyncio.run() that demonstrates full flow, error handling, and result retrieval.

steps.description: Implement single-entity AnomalyDetectorRunner with result construction and ES result indexing.
Add multi-entity support with composite aggregations and per-entity model cache.
Implement checkpoint read/write to ES for model persistence.
Write runnable example usage script with argparse, detector config, and asyncio.run().

assumptions.answer: User targets an Elasticsearch cluster (not OpenSearch) for the async client; some index/field names follow OpenSearch AD conventions (.opendistro-anomaly-*).; krcf (Python bindings for aws/random-cut-forest-by-aws) provides sufficient RCF primitives; we will implement the ThresholdedRandomCutForest wrapper (thresholding, alerting, auto-adjust) in Python.; Detector configurations and source data already exist in Elasticsearch; the Python module focuses on executing detection, not bootstrapping an entire AD plugin infrastructure.; Feature aggregations use standard Elasticsearch DSL (no OpenSearch-specific query extensions).; Shingling, imputation, and attribution mapping will be manually implemented in Python to match Java behavior, since krcf does not expose the parkservices ThresholdedRandomCutForest API.; Cold-start training data is fetched from the same source indices as real-time detection. Minimum train samples default to 512 (Java: MIN_TRAIN_SAMPLES).

payload.summary: Phase 1 complete. Established Python project foundation: requirements.txt installed, Pydantic v2 models mirroring Java AD classes, async ES client factory with retry/backoff, index management helpers, composite aggregation pagination, and pytest configuration with 9 passing tests.
